clue.text: One goes by gas or electric chair — couples on periphery of drive-by set free

definitions.text: One goes by gas or electric

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and can fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
the pairs of letters at each edge of drive-by: its first two, DR, and its last two, BY

explanation.surface: A grim scene: an execution by gas or electric chair, while partners caught up in a drive-by shooting walk free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'electric chair' reads as one phrase, but 'electric' ends the definition and 'chair' starts the fodder. 'couples' means letter pairs: DR and BY sit at the two ends of drive-by.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid vehicle runs on petrol (gas, in American English) or on battery power, switching between the two.

clue.text: Penultimate set from Aretha Franklin — kept tape for wallower

parts.note: the penultimate (second-to-last) letter of Aretha
the penultimate letter of Franklin
the penultimate letter of kept
the penultimate letter of tape
the penultimate letter of for

explanation.surface: A recording engineer keeps the tape of Aretha Franklin's second-to-last set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penultimate set from' tells you to take the second-to-last letter of each of the next five words, Aretha, Franklin, kept, tape and for, in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The river horse spends its days lolling in mud and water, the classic wallowing animal.

clue.text: Girlfriend took off, caught infection

parts.note: bird is British slang for a girlfriend

indicators.note: caught here means heard, so the word for took off is taken by its sound

parts.note: took off, as a plane or bird does, means flew

explanation.surface: A man's girlfriend left him, and then he caught something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like it belongs with infection, but it signals the sound: FLEW, said aloud, gives FLU.
explanation.definitionFit: Avian influenza is a viral illness spread among poultry and wild fowl, so it is a kind of infection.

clue.text: Steep road up and down, Lucy's first to go

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: to go means a letter departs from the word for down

parts.note: down, meaning sad, is blue

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of Lucy's

explanation.surface: Directions for a hilly road, with a note that Lucy should leave first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective about the road, but it is a verb. 'up and down' tempts as one phrase; 'up' reverses MI and 'down' is BLUE, losing its L.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it thoroughly, and to imbue is likewise to saturate or permeate.

clue.text: Schroeder back playing US game on these?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Schroeder, the Peanuts pianist, has returned to playing, perhaps a game of American draughts.
explanation.walkthrough: Schroeder is the piano-playing boy in the Peanuts strip, so 'playing' seems to mean music.
explanation.definitionFit: The American name for draughts is checkers, and the squared boards it is played on carry the matching name.

clue.text: About time, even if parts considered again

indicators.note: parts means the phrase for even if splits the other pieces, sitting between them

parts.note: re is Latin for about, as in letter headings
even if means though

explanation.surface: Some parts of a plan were reconsidered, a matter of time even so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun but is a verb: THOUGH divides RE from T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mulled over a second time has been reconsidered, a straight past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Scream — break interrupted by Munch's head that's flipped

indicators.note: interrupted by means one piece breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: hol is a short form of holiday, a break
the head of Munch is M; flipped upside down, an M looks like a W

explanation.surface: The Scream, Munch's famous painting of a figure whose head is clutched in anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: Edvard Munch painted The Scream, which feeds the surface. The letter M turned upside down becomes W.
explanation.definitionFit: A howl is a long loud cry of pain or anguish, a close synonym for a scream.

clue.text: People to take out on this bash, mostly drunk on street

definitions.text: People to take out on this

parts.note: to bash is to hit

indicators.note: mostly means the word for drunk loses its final letter

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A wild party, with people mostly drunk out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' reads as a party and 'take out' as a night out, but take out here means kill.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster's roster of targets for murder names those to be eliminated, so the people are on it.

clue.text: Star of Comedy Store festival

parts.note: Victoria Wood was a star of British comedy
a store is stock

explanation.surface: A headline act from the Comedy Store, the London club, playing a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Comedy Store is a London comedy club, but here 'Comedy' and 'Store' belong to separate pieces. Victoria Wood was a much-loved British comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1969 music festival held in upstate New York is the most famous rock festival of all; it also names Snoopy's bird friend.

clue.text: Reclining model, bare, posing a bit, could go under the knife?

indicators.note: reclining means lying back, so the letters are read backwards
a bit means only a portion of the run of words is used

explanation.surface: An artist's model lies back nude, posing, and wonders about cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reclining' looks like a pose for the model, but it turns the hidden letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient or condition fit for surgery is one that can be cut into, under the surgeon's blade.

clue.text: Ink pattern close to Peppermint Patty's outline missing circles

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter
outline missing means the outer letters of the name are dropped

parts.note: the name Patty, with its outside letters to be removed
two circles look like two letter O's

explanation.surface: Describing the pattern on Peppermint Patty, the Peanuts tomboy, with her outline drawn but no circles.
explanation.walkthrough: Peppermint Patty is a Peanuts character; the name is split between two pieces here.
explanation.definitionFit: A design inked permanently into the skin is the body art drawn by a needle.

clue.text: Sweet thing isn't introduced when meeting Charlie Brown

parts.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for a sweet thing is not brought in

parts.note: a toffee is a sweet

explanation.surface: Someone sweet who hasn't been introduced on meeting Charlie Brown, the Peanuts hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie Brown' reads as a single name, but Charlie is C and Brown is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mid-brown colour is named after the roasted bean drink, as in coffee-coloured.

clue.text: Magazines with fronts stuck together — Fiesta missing cover that's most kinky

indicators.note: two copies are placed so that their front letters meet in the middle, the first copy facing backwards

parts.note: OK! is a British celebrity magazine; the plural gives two copies
the second copy of the magazine OK!

indicators.note: missing cover means the outside letters of the word are lost

explanation.surface: Top-shelf magazines with pages glued together, and a copy of Fiesta lacking its cover: the kinkiest stash.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiesta is a British adult magazine. One OK reversed beside another makes KOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Kooky means eccentric or weird; the superlative stretches to the strangest or most perverse.

clue.text: Taunt Linus about blanket at the end

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around
at the end picks the final letter of blanket

explanation.surface: Mocking Linus, the Peanuts boy, about his security blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: Linus in the Peanuts strip always carries a security blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt someone is to jeer or offer an affront, the same act as a verbal slight.

clue.text: Sewer being awry, ran to supply

indicators.note: read as supply-ly, in a supple way, so the letters are bent into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sewer went wrong, and someone ran off to fetch supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb, but read as 'supplely' it signals the rearrangement. 'Sewer' means a dweller in the sewers, not someone sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: The brown rat is the common rodent of drains, a creature that lives in sewers.

clue.text: Part of American train track's fine

parts.note: to track someone is to tail them
fine, as in delicate, is light

explanation.surface: A section of an American railway track is in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests the railway, but in American usage it can mean a line of vehicles in a convoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The red lamp at the rear of a vehicle or train carriage is one of its components.

clue.text: Asking back to work to cut dole

indicators.note: to cut means one piece slices into another

parts.note: to dole out is to ration

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn, or to go is to work, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Pleading to be let back into work in order to cut unemployment benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dole' reads as British unemployment benefit, but here it means a share handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogation is solemn supplication or prayer, a formal kind of asking or petitioning.

clue.text: Plant one roughly on cheek

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, means the pieces it joins follow the word for cheek, placed after it

parts.note: brass is slang for cheek or nerve
I is the Roman numeral one
ca, short for circa, means roughly

explanation.surface: Planting a rough kiss on someone's cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb but is the definition noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabbage family's genus covers kale, sprouts and turnips, all of them garden vegetables.

clue.text: What am I doing in this position?

definitions.text: What am I doing in this position?

parts.words: What am I doing in this position?
parts.note: the setter, speaking as 'I', describes their own activity: composing the very puzzle, and placing this word at this spot in the grid

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in an awkward position wonders how they got there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the setter, Tramp. The answer is both what a setter does and an old word for a position or location.
explanation.definitionFit: Composing a crossword is called compiling it, and a placement or location is also its surroundings.

clue.text: Marcie running a country

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are in motion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Marcie, Peppermint Patty's friend in Peanuts, runs a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcie is a Peanuts character, the bespectacled friend who calls Peppermint Patty 'sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is the nation commonly called by the name of the continent.

clue.text: Opel nearly parked between two Ford models in Kansas city

indicators.note: parked between means the car piece is set down in the gap between two others

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's early mass-produced car
the Ka is a small Ford hatchback

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of Opel is dropped

explanation.surface: An Opel car left almost parked between two Fords in a Kansas town.
explanation.walkthrough: Opel is a German carmaker; its name here loses only its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Kansas is a city on the Kansas River.

clue.text: Bottom airbrushed from top magazine strip

indicators.note: the bottom letter of the down word for top is edited out, as in a retouched photo

parts.note: a top is a peak
Nuts was a British weekly men's magazine

explanation.surface: A top-shelf magazine has had a model's bottom airbrushed out of a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip' suggests undressing in a racy magazine, but it is the comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Schulz's long-running comic strip featured Charlie Brown and Snoopy.

clue.text: Sweet Sally cut it off during exercise

indicators.note: during means one piece is set inside another

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: off suggests the letters go wrong and are reordered
cut means the last letter of Sally is lopped off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sally stopped eating sweets during exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally is Charlie Brown's little sister in Peanuts; 'Sweet' is a noun here, a sugary lozenge, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flavoured lozenge, often fruity or medicated, is a kind of confection.

clue.text: See 4
Pig pen hot — temperature drops inside

indicators.note: drops inside means a piece falls into the middle of another

parts.note: Bic is a famous brand of ballpoint pen
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A pigsty is hot, but the temperature falls inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig pen' reads as a sty, but 'Pig' is the definition and 'pen' a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a pig or a cow is a term of abuse for a nasty, spiteful person, especially a woman.

clue.text: Deposit say collected by medics

indicators.note: collected by means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: DRS is short for doctors
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A sample, say, gathered up by doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' looks like a bank payment but is sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: The sediment that settles at the bottom of a glass or bottle is a residue.

clue.text: Difficult changing lead for Snoopy

indicators.note: changing lead means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a trying time is a difficult one

explanation.surface: A tricky time changing the lead on Snoopy, Charlie Brown's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog's leash, but it is the first letter. 'Snoopy' seems to be the Peanuts beagle; it is the adjective nosy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nosy or meddlesome is a matter of poking into others' affairs.

clue.text: Unwelcome guest in Yorkshire isn't more offensive?

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect, isn't is often said as int
more offensive means ruder

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: isn't an unwelcome guest even more offensive in Yorkshire?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Yorkshire' looks like a location for the guest, but it qualifies 'isn't': Yorkshire speech shortens it to INT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enters without invitation or permission is an unwanted visitor.

clue.text: Kind of party animal

definitions.meaning: a night out for a groom-to-be before the wedding

explanation.surface: A party animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor party is named for the male deer, and a male deer is an animal.

clue.text: Boxes with pain during matches

indicators.note: during means one piece occurs inside another

parts.note: Tests are international cricket matches
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A boxer fights with pain during his matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like a verb for fighting but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Large wooden crates originally used to ship tea are standard containers for moving house.
